Initialise the title tune and VIC raster interrupt, set KERNAL keyboard repeat and queue limits, and point RESTORE at this entry so it can restart the game.

Select VIC bank $8000, blank the border, load eight sprite coordinate and colour pairs, expand the title, colour the character cells, and wait for joystick input or F1 while changing the sprite animation.
The title polls KERNAL matrix index $04 for F1. It suppresses sprites and invokes the password form before entering the new-level path.
Port 2 is read through CIA1 port A. The title animation keeps looping when the idle value is $7F.
Reset per-level counters and expand the maze selected by $7D37 into $6000. Initialise the status digits, then scan the maze for actor starting cells.

The indexed maze scan reads $6032 through $6570 using Y=$31 and operand bases $6001 through $653F. Save unindexed bases for tile $45 and tile $04, replace $FF with $02, and record the coordinates of tile $03.
Low operand of the scanning LDA at $3746, incremented across each map cell.
High byte of the self-modifying map read used to scan for initial positions. Incremented with carry when $3747 wraps.
Low byte of the store address patched to the page offset of the spawn marker.
High byte of the patched store addressing a detected $FF marker. The scan writes tile $02 over that marker before continuing.
Call the viewport builder and return. This entry is called before the first input poll of the level.
Rebuild the viewport and jump back to the input loop.
Rebuild the viewport's character buffer from the middle of the drawing routine for one fine-scroll step.
Run the death sequence and decrement remaining lives at $3845. Display the life-lost screen if a life remains and branch to game over otherwise.
A second absolute jump to $36EB immediately follows the one at $38A0.
Copy the saved maze from $C000 back into the live maze at $6001. Restore actor positions, inventory and panel cells from their saved values before returning to the level setup.
Low operand of the maze restore source at $38BA, stepped forward from zero.
Page operand of the restore source, initially $C0 and increased after the low source wraps.
Low operand of the maze restore destination. Starts at one and steps with the source byte.
High store operand for the maze restore at $38BD. The loop increments its source and destination together and stops when the latter reaches $6580.
Expand screen record 1 and refresh its colours. Start the title tune and wait for joystick input before redrawing the title.
Run the score dispatch before checking the function-key matrix index. Index $05 restarts, $06 sets the death flag and $03 waits for port 2 input.
Read port 2. Set bit 4 in A before dispatch so the directional comparisons work with either fire state. The collision handler reads the actual fire bit again for mould.
Reset idle animation counters and compare the direction bits with the four single-direction codes. Pass the neighbour offset in Y to $3CC4 and animate a step only if it returns nonzero.
Decrement the pending animation count when nonzero and use it as an index into $7B96 to update sprite pointer 0.
Immediate sprite pointer used on the odd branch of the two-frame toggle for sprite six.
Parked sprite value used on the even branch of the object animation toggle. The goblin routine can amend it along with $3AED.
Compute the visible origin from the scrolling row and column at $7C56 and $7C57. Build a 7 by 11 tile work area from the map starting at $6001.
Reset destination to $7000, then look up the 16-byte character pattern of each visible tile using the split pointer table at $7600 and $767A. Copy each as four rows of four character codes.
Low address of the current tile's sixteen-byte matrix, patched from the split low table.
High byte of the matrix fetch, patched from the tile's high-address lookup.
Low byte of the current work-buffer write in the tile copier.
Destination page for the work-buffer tile copy. Each group of four advances by $2C and the end of a tile backs it up by $80.
Use the fine offsets to select a 36 by 20 character window from the work area. Copy each row to $8402 with 40-byte screen stride and map the characters through $8300 to colour RAM.
Low origin of the source buffer cell read by the viewport.
Patched high source page in the viewport blit, advanced when adding its 44-byte row stride carries.
Low screen destination at $3BFA, advanced by 40 on each visible line.
High byte of the viewport destination in screen RAM, advanced when adding the 40-cell screen stride crosses a page.
Low colour RAM destination, advanced by the same 40 cells as the screen.
High operand of the viewport colour store. The loop advances it when adding 40 to the low operand wraps.
Count 255 Y increments for each of 100 X iterations, then return. Callers use this same delay between changes to the display.
Load zero into A and return. The next routine starts at $3C49.
Poll CIA1 port A in a bounded nested loop. Return A=1 for a sample below $70 and A=0 if the wait expires.

Construct the biased maze pointer from the player coordinates. Probe offsets $30, $5F, $5F, $61 and $90 for tile $05 and compare offset zero with zero by default. The movement profile can patch the final offset and tile test. Set $7C66 when a probe matches.
Immediate maze probe offset selecting the final hazard cell, patched from the profile table at $7C9C.
Tile value compared in the last hazard test against the current cell. The active movement profile patches it at $4217.

Compute the maze address from Bono's position and the neighbour offset in Y. Dispatch by the target tile, update tile and inventory bytes where appropriate, and return a nonzero A when Bono may advance.
Tile $0E spends five skeletons and produces one soap when there is sufficient stock and fewer than nine soaps. Queue score place three and redraw the inventory. Return zero so Bono stays in place.
Tile $12 becomes cleared ground when fewer than nine skeletons are carried. Raise the skeleton count, queue score place two and allow Bono to step into the cell.
Tile $10 becomes cleared ground if the key count is below nine. Increment the key count, queue score place two and return one to allow movement.
Tile $0F requires a carried key. Spend one, change the gate into tile $01, queue score place three and keep Bono in place on the opening tick.
Tile $02 is cleared to $03 and passable without fire. With the lower port sample, replace it by $01 and return zero so Bono clears the neighbour from his current cell.
Convert the counters for keys, soaps and skeletons into screen digits at $87CF, $87BC and $87CC. Restore the entry test result as A=1 if X was saved as one and zero otherwise.
Map each of the 1000 screen cells at $8400 through the 256-byte colour table at $C800 into colour RAM, in four runs of 250 cells.
For the direction in $7C61, step the corresponding sub-tile offset towards one or seven and draw each intermediate frame through $3829. Return the offset to four.
Set sprite enable according to the current maze cell, test hazards, then walk the maze by 48-byte rows looking for moving tiles. Update the bonus digits during this scan when the bonus flag is set.
Low source address for the maze LDA patched to the cell derived from the $FF marker.
High byte of the maze operand patched to the effective $FF marker's address. Setup adds Y=$31 to the unindexed scan operand.
Low operand of the second marker-cell write in the sprite enabling branch.
High byte patched to the maze address found by the level setup. A nominated cell with value one becomes six when the additional sprite is enabled.
Immediate operand for the neighbour read during the moving tile comparison at $4068. The motion configuration indexes its source at $7C6C.
Immediate offset for the first new Glook marker. Patched by $41DB before the maze update loop uses it.
Immediate offset for the second probe of the first pair of adjacent cells.
Immediate value for the Glook's first new marker after a neighbouring pair passes its empty-cell tests.
Immediate new cell value for the first moving Glook candidate, selected by the movement profile at $41FA.
Immediate offset for the first candidate on the Glook's other side. Loaded from $7C80 for the current profile.
Immediate offset for the second checked cell on the other side of the Glook.
Immediate value for the Glook's other new marker, assigned before storing to offset $409D.
Replacement tile for the second moving Glook candidate. The profile initializer takes it from $7C94.
Tile placed beside the Glook when the first neighbouring cell matches tile one, based on the active movement profile.
Immediate operand set by the active maze-motion table. This branch updates the second marker after moving the neighbouring tile.
Active movement profile copied from $4959. It selects offsets for cells surrounding the creature tile.
Clear the panel bonus digits and apply the parameter tables indexed by $4959. Patch neighbour offsets and tile codes in the motion and hazard routines before the next scan.
Check tile $04 at the current actor pointer and test neighbours using offsets selected by the direction index. Its counter in $7CA5 controls the countdown step that can leave a skeleton.
First neighbour lookup offset. Copied from the active facing index in $7CA8.
The second neighbour probe uses the direction-dependent offset from $7CAC.
The third direction candidate copied from $7CB0 and used by the next load from the maze pointer.
Last of four patched neighbour offsets at $424C, $425E, $426D and here. The probes distinguish tile one and tile five before the actor and its timer are updated.

Check tile $45 at the actor pointer, then test four surrounding cells in a direction-dependent order. Tile $03 requests a player death. The other passable cases write a pair of animation tiles and adjust the pointer.
Immediate offset of the initial spider probe, patched from the facing-direction table at $7CBB.
Second spider probe offset, selected from $7CBF with the same facing index.
Third comparison offset for spider movement. $43B7 fills it from the array at $7CC3.
Last of four patched offsets in the spider's neighbour probes. The branch compares that cell with the same three tile codes as the preceding three checks.
Read $4541 as a decimal place selector. Values one through five increment units through ten-thousands, with carry through the displayed decimal digits. Clear the request after handling it.
Select the displayed digit to increment. Zero means no scoring request. Mould, pickups, kettle and deliveries write selectors one, two, three and four.
Save the eight sprite pointers, position registers and sprite colours for restoration after an interlude.
Patch copy operands to preserve the maze beginning at $6001 in the scratch buffer at $C000. Save pointer, inventory and score fields for the restore path.
Low byte of the map-save source, starting at the second byte of the expanded map.
High operand of the load that advances across level cells while copying them to the backup buffer.
Low operand of the copy into the $C000 snapshot used after a delivery.
High byte of the $C000 save address, patched by the copy loop when the low byte wraps.
Restore all eight sprite pointers from $7CF7, positions from $7CFF and colours from $7D0F.

Expand screen record 7, collect letters or spaces from GETIN with Delete editing, and compare twelve screen codes with successive entries at $CB40 after subtracting $36. A failed scan falls back to level 1.
Low byte of the password comparison source, advanced by twelve after a mismatch.
High operand of the password table read at $466F, advanced when adding twelve to the low byte carries.

Select the twelve-byte password record for the next maze, subtract $36 from each byte, and copy the result into the password award screen. Patch the source addresses for the artwork matching the panel digits.
Low operand of the player-facing password print. $46B3 steps it to the selected record.
High operand of the load at $46DA, paired with the low byte amended for the next level's password.
Low starting address of the first award image strip's source.
Page operand of the first password award strip source, selected through the table at $49A4.

Low starting address of the second award image strip's source.

Value patched from the second digit's glyph mapping at $4B03.
Choose X=0 in the $6CE8 music driver, switch the upper display base operand to $18 and set the raster IRQ.
Choose X=1 in the $6CE8 music driver, select upper display base $1F and install the raster IRQ.
Choose X=1 in the $9E5E music driver, select upper display base $1F and install the raster IRQ.
Choose X=0 in the $9E5E music driver, select upper display base $18 and install the raster IRQ.
Save maze and sprites, set the seven sprite positions and shapes for screen record 3 and wait for fire. On the fifth delivery display the password before the level advances.
Reset the level selector and draw screen record 6. Overlay the password-free congratulation line only when the password flag is clear and wait for a joystick action.
Copy four alternate bitmap pointer values from $7D33 to the first four raster sprite slots.
Replace the first four pointers with the scene's base values at $7D2C.
Preserve the gameplay sprite state. Set up the bath sprites, display the bathing screen, and count the delivered soap. On the fifth delivery show the next password and advance the level.
Copy six sprite pointers from $7D5A to $87FA during the timed input wait.
Copy the second set of six pointers from $7D60 to restore the other side of the bath animation.
Write the displayed lives, retry, level and inventory digits. Convert the internal level index from base 8 to the display's base 1 and show deliveries still required as five minus $7D38.
Converted to the left digit of the panel's retry counter. Crossing zero forces one life and raises the death request.
Set to five at the title and decremented at $3845 with the trainer disabled. Its zero test chooses the game-over path.
Scan column counter, incremented until it reaches the row width of 48.
Stored spawn column, copied to the player's current column during level setup.
Scan row counter, incremented after the end of each 48-cell row.
Stored spawn row from the maze scan, copied to the current player grid row.
Selected maze-motion profile. Copied into $41AB by $41B8 before patching its movement cases.

Eight bytes copied to $D027 through $D02E for the title sprites.
Count of characters entered into the twelve-byte password field.
Preserved low byte of the spider actor pointer after delivery.
Preserved high byte of the spider actor pointer.

Saved skeleton count from the interlude backup.

Low addresses selected by the second panel digit for copying 30 character codes onto the award screen.
High-byte partner of the second digit's picture source pointer.
Low byte table for the first 30-character frame selected by the displayed first digit.
High address table for the first 30-byte glyph strip on the password award screen. The panel digit indexes this table at $46F3.
Stored character codes for the bathing-monster remarks, including PULL THE PLUG OUT, WELL DONE BONO and WHAT A MAN. Includes artwork and spacing glyphs between the messages.
Caption glyph values for the second strip selected by the second panel digit. One value patches the instruction operand at $472E.
Caption glyph values selected by the first panel digit and stored into the operand at $4709.
Set to one when the title enters the password form. The completion sequence reads it before copying its extra congratulation line.
Twenty-eight stored glyph codes. Subtract $17 from each and copy them to the finishing screen at $86D6 when the run has no password flag.
Raster animation source at $5880. The pointer tables at $CAFF and $CB17 pair this 128-byte frame with destination $A000. Each frame supplies sixteen 8-byte glyphs.

Raster animation source at $5980. The pointer tables at $CAFF and $CB17 pair this 128-byte frame with destination $A100. Each frame supplies sixteen 8-byte glyphs.

Sixteen eight-row bitmaps in the same storage layout as the adjoining raster frames. The rendered rows show connected silhouettes and linework. The twelve-entry animation table does not point directly here.
Raster animation source at $5A80. The pointer tables at $CAFF and $CB17 pair this 128-byte frame with destination $A100. Each frame supplies sixteen 8-byte glyphs.
